proposed.explanation:
TMGH shows strong fundamental momentum that aligns well with your aggressive, long-horizon profile. Net income attributable to parent shareholders grew from 9,025,066,065 EGP in 2024 to 14,383,890,306 EGP in 2025, a roughly 59% year-over-year increase. EPS rose from 4.38 to 6.98 EGP over the same period, confirming the earnings growth is not just a share-count effect. Gross profit expanded about 49% (14.00 B → 20.86 B EGP), and total equity grew 21% to 157.71 B EGP, indicating the company is reinvesting and building a larger balance sheet.

At the current price of 82.50 EGP, the trailing P/E is approximately 11.8× (82.50 / 6.98), which is reasonable for a company growing earnings at ~59%. You are not paying a premium multiple for the growth.

You currently hold 100 shares of EFID (2,040 EGP) and 40,000 EGP in cash, for a total portfolio of 42,040 EGP. Buying 250 shares of TMGH costs 20,625 EGP, leaving 19,375 EGP in cash. After the purchase, TMGH would represent about 49.1% of the portfolio—just under the 50% diversification cap—while EFID stays at ~4.9% and cash at ~46.1%. This keeps you diversified across two equities plus a meaningful cash buffer.

Risks and caveats: (1) The evidence covers only one fiscal year of growth; a single-year spike does not guarantee a 10-year trend. (2) I have no financial evidence on EFID, so I am not recommending you sell or add to it—just holding it as-is. (3) A P/E of ~12× can compress if growth slows, and the Egyptian market carries currency, regulatory, and macro risks. (4) The 2024 figures are restated, so the growth rate may be slightly overstated relative to originally reported numbers. Given your high risk tolerance, 10+ year horizon, and no liquidity needs, a concentrated position in a high-growth name is appropriate, but this is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
